reviews.title: As described, new condition and works fantastic.
reviews.comment: Works great!  Much rather purchase this over the RTX 3090 Nvidia price gouging machine.  After a bios upgrade to my mainboard all is good.  Going from an GTX 1070 to an RX 6900 XT was a fricken wakeup call.  No regrets.  I think I'll be switching the rest of my hardware over to AMD as well and the fact all of the new generation consoles are rocking AMD hardware PC builders will most likely benefit largely from this.

reviews.title: Great card that is too expensive.
reviews.comment: Absolutely love it. My first GPU manufactured with the AMD architecture. Have always bought the highest end Nvidia based GPU's in the past. With prices being what they are I decided to see what AMD had up there sleeves. And am very pleased with my decision. For literally half the price (though still quite pricey) I got a GPU that rivals the Nvidia rtx 3090.
reviews.author: Brian D. Williamson

reviews.title: This is a 6900xt XTXH Aircooled
reviews.comment:
Pros:
Clocks at 2450mhz with no fuss.
Installation was a breeze
Haven't found much need to OC in the games I play. As performance is excellent.
Cold War, WarZone, Division, Valhalla, Deathloop, Battlefied 5, etc run flawlessly and smooth.
Received promotional free games without issue.  It did take a few days.
Temps are decent for air cool. Junction temps: roughly 85C+. Edge temps roughly 60c. At 2500mhz +.
Radeon Software is great. I've been using that more.
Cons:
MSI Afterburner Voltage Control didn't work. I had to copy and paste a set of commands into a Profile File "VEN_..." found in the Profile sub directory of MSI Afterburner folder to get it to recognize my gpu voltage.  It reset the file which recognize this card. Using the Checkbox "Unlock voltage monitoring" and rebooting did not work.  Nor did tweaking the MSIAfterburner.cfg.  This wasn't a problem with my other card. This is important because MSI Afterburner Software is showcased as the Software for this video card.
This thing does get warm if you don't have good airflow.
It does require a brace of some kind to prevent sagging.
Not clear on how to control the RBG effects on the card.  Not much of a con for me though.
Notes:
You do need to use the bracket to keep it from sagging.  I couldn't use it because I had another pcie device plugged in. So I had to improvise. Not much of a con but worth noting.
Max OC is about 2600mhz.  Anything higher requires a water block.
The card is taller then most.  So, screwing it into the chassis will be a bit tighter
Keep in mind this requires 3 (not 2) pcie connectors.
If MSI reads this please invest in making a waterblock for this gpu (6900xt Gaming Trio Z). This card has more potential if keep cool.
